sentences.text: This Crl.M.C. under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is filed by accused Nos.1 to 4 in Crime No.809 of 2021 of Mala Police Station, Thrissur District, registered under Sections 498A and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 for quashing Annexure-A1 final report in C.C.No.106 of 2022, on the file of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chalakudy.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chalakudy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The prosecution allegation is that, the petitioners, who are the husband, children and daughter-in- law of the defacto complainant, subjected her to physical and mental torture demanding money and gold ornaments.

3. When the matter is taken up for consideration, learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that, the matter stands settled between the petitioners and the 3rd respondent, who is the defacto complainant.

The petitioners have produced affidavit of the 3rd respondent, which shows that the matter has been settled, and she has no intention to continue with the prosecution, and she has no objection in quashing the proceedings in C.C.No.106 of 2022 pending against the petitioners, before Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chalakudy.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-I, Chalakudy
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
4. Learned Public Prosecutor, on instructions, submitted that, the matter has been settled between parties, and he produced signed statement of the 3rd respondent, asserting that the matter has been amicably settled, and the 3rd respondent has no objection in quashing the proceedings in C.C.No.106 of 2022.
Joseph vs State Of Kerala on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49978248/

5. Since the matter stands settled, no purpose would be served by continuing the prosecution against the petitioners.

6. In the light of the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another; [(2012) 10 SCC 303)], and State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others; [(2019)
5 SCC 688], this Court is of the view that the proceedings against the petitioners can be quashed on the basis of settlement.
